uncited: This family is distinguished from direct volume rendering methods by producing a discrete geometric representation (mesh) suitable for standard rasterization pipelines, ray tracing, or physical simulation, whereas volume rendering computes pixel colors directly from scalar fields [1-volume-rendering.md].

[Isosurface extraction](30-isosurface-extraction.md) All methods in this family operate on a discretized domain, typically a regular grid (Cartesian, octree, or tetrahedral) where each cell contains scalar values or occupancy states at its vertices or centers.
**Surface Determination**: A criterion is applied to identify surface locations.
In isosurface methods, this involves comparing scalar values against a threshold (isovalue) to detect sign changes or equality [30-isosurface-extraction.md].
In blocky meshing, this involves checking occupancy states or material IDs to identify exposed boundaries [31-blocky-meshing.md].
**Mesh Coherence**: Adjacent primitives are merged or connected to form a coherent mesh, often requiring vertex merging to avoid duplicates and ensure watertightness [30-isosurface-extraction.md].
